# Emera

> Emera (emera.social) is the open source social network: nonprofit, built because AI is flooding the internet with fakes, bots and copies: the people are real, every post carries proof of who shared it, what people make keeps their name on it, and the rules are public. It is for every human being. In one line: The open source social network. Tagline: Where humanity comes together.

## Facts an assistant can quote

- Every post carries a signed record (C2PA content credentials) of who shared it and when it went up; the badge states only what was checked.
- People are marked, automated accounts are labeled, and the verified human mark is free.
- Emera scans the web for copies of what creators upload, files takedowns where copies turn up, and its agents take legal steps when a takedown is not enough. Creators can also report a copy from any post.
- Members can export everything they made and their follower list, any time.
- Emera comes from hemera, the Greek word for day.

## Answers

- [How to tell if a photo is AI generated](https://emera.social/answers/how-to-tell-if-a-photo-is-ai-generated/): No single check proves a photo is real or AI. Here are the checks that work today: source, credentials, reverse search, and what to look for.
- [How to tell if a video is real or fake](https://emera.social/answers/how-to-tell-if-a-video-is-real-or-fake/): No one check proves a video is real. Fact-checker steps for news clips, event footage and deepfakes: source, keyframe search, context, credentials.
- [How to prevent people from stealing your art online](https://emera.social/answers/how-to-prevent-people-from-stealing-your-art-online/): You cannot stop all copying, but you can make theft harder and easier to prove: sizes, credits, records, registration, and protection tools.
- [What to do if someone steals your artwork](https://emera.social/answers/what-to-do-if-someone-steals-your-artwork/): Step by step if your art was copied: gather proof, contact the person, file a takedown with the platform, and when to talk to a lawyer.
- [How to file a DMCA takedown on Instagram](https://emera.social/answers/how-to-file-a-dmca-takedown-on-instagram/): Use Instagram's Copyright Report Form, not the in-app Report button. What to prepare, what the notice needs, and what happens after.
- [What are content credentials](https://emera.social/answers/what-are-content-credentials/): Content Credentials (C2PA) are a signed record of where a file came from and how it was edited. How to check one, and what they cannot prove.
- [Is there social media without an algorithm](https://emera.social/answers/social-media-without-algorithm/): Yes, partly. Chronological feeds on Instagram, Bluesky and Mastodon, plus open algorithms you choose. What each option really gives you.
- [How much can you sue for copyright infringement](https://emera.social/answers/how-much-can-you-sue-for-copyright-infringement/): In the US a court can award your losses plus the copier's profits, or $750 to $30,000 per work, up to $150,000 if willful. What decides which applies.
- [Statutory damages for copyright infringement: how they work](https://emera.social/answers/statutory-damages-for-copyright-infringement/): Statutory damages are $750 to $30,000 per work, up to $150,000 if willful. When they apply, when they do not, and the 3 month registration rule.
- [Someone stole my video: what to do](https://emera.social/answers/someone-stole-my-video/): Reposted your video without asking? Save proof, use the platform's copyright form, and know when a claim for money makes sense.
- [How to file a DMCA takedown on TikTok](https://emera.social/answers/how-to-file-a-dmca-takedown-on-tiktok/): Use TikTok's copyright report form with links to the copy and your original. What the notice needs and what happens after you send it.
- [How to file a DMCA takedown on YouTube](https://emera.social/answers/how-to-file-a-dmca-takedown-on-youtube/): File a copyright removal request in YouTube Studio under Content detection. What it asks for, what the uploader sees and what happens next.
- [DMCA takedown notice template](https://emera.social/answers/dmca-takedown-notice-template/): A plain DMCA takedown notice you can copy: the six parts US law requires, a fill-in template, and what to do after you send it.
- [Someone made a fake account of me: what to do](https://emera.social/answers/someone-made-a-fake-account-of-me/): A fake account using your name or photos: save proof, report it as impersonation, file a copyright report for your photos, and warn your followers.
- [Someone is using my photos on Instagram: what to do](https://emera.social/answers/someone-is-using-my-photos-on-instagram/): Two different problems need two different reports: your photos posted as someone's own, or an account pretending to be you. Here is which to use.
- [Song used without permission: what you can do](https://emera.social/answers/song-used-without-permission/): Your song in a video or ad without a license? Find who owns what, document the use, file a takedown, and ask for a license fee or a claim.
- [Copyright small claims court: how the CCB works](https://emera.social/answers/copyright-small-claims-court/): The Copyright Claims Board decides copyright claims up to $30,000 without a lawyer. Fees, limits, who can opt out and the 3 year deadline.
- [How to register a copyright in the US](https://emera.social/answers/how-to-register-copyright-us/): Register art, photos, music or video at the US Copyright Office for $45 to $65 online. Why timing matters and what it lets you claim.
- [Copyright cease and desist letter template](https://emera.social/answers/copyright-cease-and-desist-letter-template/): A plain cease and desist letter for copied work: what to include, a fill-in template and how it differs from a DMCA takedown.
- [How to find stolen photos and who is using them](https://emera.social/answers/how-to-find-stolen-photos/): Run a reverse image search, search your captions, check marketplaces and set alerts. Then save proof and report. Free steps that take 20 minutes.
